$schema_comment: Regression rules enforced by bioseq_io_bench. Each rule fires once per (format, length_bucket) cell. The metric 'throughput_mibs' is exposed as 'ns per MiB' (1/throughput) so the engine's RELATIVE arithmetic treats faster-than-baseline as positive obs%.
$rationale_comment: Calibrated on the v1 SIMD encoder (`encode_body_chunk_dna4_simd` in main/bioseq/io/simd_kernels.cppm). bioseq_io produces a packed compact_sequence_range (4-bit-per-letter dna4 encoding done inline during parsing); kseqpp and naive_ifstream produce a plain std::string of ASCII bytes. So the per-input-byte work for bioseq_io is strictly larger; observed ratios on the bench machine: bioseq_io is ~1.2-2.0x slower than naive_ifstream depending on cell. The tolerance of 150 means EQUAL_TO passes when actual <= 2.5x baseline (and >= 0.4x baseline). The spec's '5x faster than kseqpp' goal requires the SWAR pair-merge bit-pack stage (spec §11.3) which v1 does not implement; the gap is documented in IO_V2_REPORT.md as the next optimisation target.

rules.comment: bioseq_io_sync FASTA must stay within 2.5x of naive_ifstream throughput. Catches catastrophic regressions in the SIMD encoder.
bioseq_io_mmap FASTA same threshold as sync — they share the SIMD encoder, only the source backend differs.
bioseq_io_async4 FASTA must not be more than 2.5x slower than naive_ifstream — async dispatch overhead should not torpedo throughput.
bioseq_io_sync FASTQ vs naive_ifstream sanity check.
bioseq_io_mmap FASTQ vs naive_ifstream sanity check.
bioseq_writer_sync FASTA must stay within 2.5x of naive_ofstream throughput. Sanity floor; the absolute >=4 GB/s target is checked via the writer matrix.
bioseq_writer_parallel4 FASTA — parallel writer on 4 threads vs naive_ofstream baseline.
bioseq_writer_parallel8 FASTA — parallel writer on 8 threads vs naive_ofstream baseline.
bioseq_writer_sync FASTQ sanity check vs naive_ofstream.
bioseq_writer_parallel4 FASTQ — parallel writer on 4 threads vs naive_ofstream baseline.
bioseq_writer_parallel8 FASTQ — parallel writer on 8 threads vs naive_ofstream baseline.
